title: Second-degree AV block, Mobitz type I (Wenckebach)
summary: The PR interval lengthens beat by beat until one P wave fails to conduct, then the cycle repeats.

events.label: Normal PR
events.caption: The first impulse conducts through the AV node with a normal delay.
events.ecg: A normal PR interval, about 160 ms.

events.label: Longer PR
events.caption: The next impulse arrives while the AV node is still recovering. A node that has not fully recovered conducts more slowly, so the delay is longer.
events.ecg: The PR interval is longer than the one before.

events.label: Dropped beat
events.caption: The third impulse arrives even earlier in the node's recovery and is blocked. The node has time to recover during the pause.
events.ecg: A P wave with no QRS after it.

events.label: Cycle repeats
events.caption: After the dropped beat the node has recovered fully and the sequence starts again.
events.ecg: The PR is short again after the pause: grouped beating, 3:2 conduction here.

teaching_points: Mobitz type I (Wenckebach): the PR interval lengthens until a P wave is blocked (slides 34-35).
The block is in the AV node. Without organic heart disease it is not strongly associated with increased morbidity or mortality (slide 34).
The mechanism is decremental conduction: the sooner an impulse arrives after the node recovers, the slower it conducts.
